title: Privacy-banded pricing pilot with automated subprocessor attestations
creator: Mariana Lopez
description: Pilot a new pricing and contract UX that groups customers into configurable 'privacy bands' (standard / protected / regulated) and automates subprocessor attestations and dynamic SCC inclusion to reduce manual contract negotiation overhead. The experiment ties a pricing delta and contract clause bundle to each band and exposes a self-serve flow for customers to request higher-band commitments and to surface subprocessor details with attestation flags.
background: Enterprise customers frequently request different combinations of data residency, retention, and subprocessor commitments. Current approach requires manual legal review for many permutations, increases sales cycles, and creates variability in pricing. We want to validate whether a banded contract+pricing model plus automated attestation for subprocessors reduces time-to-contract and preserves legal risk controls.
experiment_design: Create three privacy bands: Standard (default, no extra residency), Protected (additional SCCs + 3rd-party subprocessors vetted, +10% price), Regulated (EU/UK residency, SCC auto-activation, explicit retention SLAs, +25% price). Build a self-serve UI in the Console where customers choose/request a band and complete an automated subprocessor attestation checklist. On request, route to legal review only if a high-risk subprocessor or custom retention request is flagged. Track funnel: selection -> attestation completion -> contract signed -> time-to-close.
acceptance_criteria: Console flow built and gated behind feature flag
Automated subprocessor attestation stored in audit log and surfaced in contract PDF
SCC clause auto-inserted for requests in Protected/Regulated bands for EU/UK customers
Pilot reduces median time-to-contract from our baseline by >= 20% for participating accounts
Legal involvement reduced to <30% of band-change requests in the pilot group
success_metrics: Percentage of band-change requests requiring manual legal review
ARR uplift for customers choosing Protected/Regulated bands
Net promoter score delta for pilot accounts regarding contract friction
Number of escalations due to undisclosed subprocessors
risks: Legal: automated attestation may not be sufficient for high-risk subprocessors; need fallback
Compliance: SCC auto-insertion must be correct by jurisdiction; mistake could cause exposure
Sales: perception of forced upsell if bands are framed as pay-for-compliance
Engineering: audit logging and contract PDF merging are nontrivial and may delay rollout
Customer confusion if UI does not clearly explain implications of each band
decisions: Start pilot with US and EU-based accounts only
Use existing DPA/SCC templates but add metadata flags for auto-insert logic
Price delta targets: +10% Protected, +25% Regulated (subject to legal review)
Route any request that mentions on-prem or air-gapped storage to manual intake
